reviewFindingsClosed.finding: important - mutation.go re-anchored at the quote's nearest occurrence even where the mark is not allowed, so an upload that only added a copy of anchored text was refused 400 with advice that drops the user's new text.
reviewFindingsClosed.closed: QuoteFinder.NearestFirst lists every match in the order Find with near chooses among them, and the re-anchor loop takes the next occurrence whenever the writer answers ErrMarkNotAllowed, refusing only when none allows the mark. Verified on the real surface at three builds (proof entry 1) and by the new service test. A refused occurrence writes nothing before it is refused: MarkWriter.Mark runs the range, mark-type, attribute-nesting and markAllowedInTextblock checks over every span the range covers before its first Format call (pmdoc/find.go:1109-1147), so the retry starts from a clean fragment - I read that rather than assuming it.

reviewFindingsClosed.closed: The decision is now one function, reanchorError, which returns ErrInvalidMarkdown for a *pmdoc.MarkNotAllowedError on a mark type an open anchor carries and a plain ErrDocSchema - not documentSchemaError, so no route offers to repair a stored tree - for every other cause. TestAReanchorErrorIsTheCallersOnlyWhenTheMarkIsNotAllowed pins both outcomes, and I ran it: the invalid-markdown case asserts it is not ErrDocSchema, and each of the three server causes asserts a plain ErrDocSchema that is neither ErrDocOutsideSchema nor ErrInvalidMarkdown.

proof.criterion: The re-anchor decision: the nearest occurrence that may carry the mark, and a refusal classed as the caller's only for a mark the schema allows nowhere the quote stands
proof.surface: pmdoc's quote finder and mark writer over a real CRDT document, and docs.reanchorError over each cause the loop can carry; and the real docs.Service on a live room for the service-level cases
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/ -run 'TestNearestFirstListsEveryMatchInFindsOrderOfChoice|TestAMarkNotAllowedWhereItsTextStandsIsTheOnlyErrMarkNotAllowed' -count=1; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=… go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run 'TestAnUploadMovingAnAnchorsQuoteWhereItsMarkIsNotAllowedIsRefused|TestAnUploadCopyingAnAnchorsQuoteWhereItsMarkIsNotAllowedKeepsTheAnchorOnTheOriginal|TestAReanchorErrorIsTheCallersOnlyWhenTheMarkIsNotAllowed' -count=1 -v
proof.observed: All pass, every subtest. NearestFirst's first range is Find's answer for the same near, the rest are ordered nearer-first and, as near, earlier-first, and a quote that matches nothing is ErrTargetNotFound. Place() gives 'a code block' and 'the front matter', and an unknown mark type and an empty range stay ErrSchema that is not ErrMarkNotAllowed. At the service: the two copy cases leave the mark on the original textblock (heading, paragraph), the two move cases are ErrInvalidMarkdown that is neither ErrDocSchema nor ErrDocOutsideSchema and leave the room's tree as it was, and reanchorError answers ErrInvalidMarkdown for the sentinel alone and a plain ErrDocSchema for a refused mark type, an unreadable fragment and a mark type no open anchor carries.
proof.negativeControl: The three server causes are the control for the classification: each is a cause the loop could carry, and each is refused the caller's label and given a plain ErrDocSchema instead. None is reachable over HTTP, by design - every mark in a room was written through this same writer against the same closed type set, and the scratch document holds only the tree the upload's own markdown made - so the unit lock is where that rule can be pinned at all.
